newsitem.title: USA: N. Korean apology could open doors to other deals.
newsitem.headline: N. Korean apology could open doors to other deals.

text.p: The apology from North Korea for the intrusion of a spy submarine could lead the way to a series of diplomatic deals on nuclear reactors, food aid and eventual talks between the two Koreas, according to envoys in New York and Washington.

North Korea apologised for the first time on Sunday for an incursion by one of its submarines into South Korea in September, expressing "deep regret" in a statement that was hammered out with U.S. diplomats.
U.S. and North Korean officials have been negotiating the wording of an apology in New York since Dec. 9.
The statement, carried by the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) and monitored in Tokyo, promised no repetitions of the incident.
The submarine incident had scuttled a process of engagement intended to bring North Korea out of its isolation, revamp its nuclear programme and help ease its famine.
The apology could result in the following measures, according to officials and diplomats close to the talks.

-- A pledge from South Korea to resume construction work in the next few months on two civilian nuclear reactors in the North and a simultaneous promise from North Korea to resume canning or sealing spent nuclear fuel rods.

The South Koreans were supposed to have gone to the site in November as part of a l994 landmark accord, in which North Korea agreed to give up its suspected atomic weapons programme in exchange for oil and a set of light-water reactors. When they put the project on hold, North Korea stopped canning its rods, required by the 1994 pact.

-- South Korea has informally blocked further food aid to the North, suffering from famine after two consecutive years of serious flooding. The U.N. World Food Programme in the next few weeks plans to issue another appeal, at which time the United States may pledge about $6 million worth of food aid. In addition Washington could issue a license to allow the Cargill grain company to export a reported 500,000 tons worth of food in a barter transaction it is seeking.

-- Another initiative at risk because of the submarine incident was a proposal for four-party peace talks, involving the United States, the two Koreas and China. Both Koreas originally were reluctant to participate, but North Korea recently had begun moving toward accepting a "briefing" on the proposals from the United States and South Korea. The North wants pre-conditions, such as lifting of trade sactions and help on food aid.
But diplomats said they did not believe this would be part of an immediate package but rather would be dealt with separately after other measures were enacted.

The apology was a major concession for North Korea, which had insisted the submarine in September accidently drifted into South Korean territory. South Korea says it was on a spy mission when it broke down.

Some 26 North Korean commando went ashore, 24 were shot and killed, one was captured alive and one is still on the loose. Thirteen South Korean soldiers and civilians were killed during the hunt for the North Koreans.
